# Thereabouts MCP tools and results

## Pack families

Each family is an installable pack that answers one kind of question. Forward families use the `core` pack, when installed, for city and timezone detail.

### `core`

Reverse geocoding and city names. A latitude and longitude, or an H3 cell, gives country, subdivision, city and timezone; a town or city name gives the matching cities.

- Tools: `reverse`, `h3`, `geocode`
- Inputs: Coordinates in WGS84 degrees; an H3 cell of resolution 0 to 8 as 15 hexadecimal characters; a city name of at most 128 normalized characters.
- Built from tables: `cells`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`, `timezone_cells`, `zone_tables`
- Notes: Every other family reads the core pack for city and timezone detail when it is installed. geocode finds towns and cities, never street addresses.

### `postal`

Postal code to place.

- Tools: `postal`
- Inputs: A code and the country it belongs to. Codes repeat across countries, so the country is required. Spaces are ignored; hyphens and leading zeros are kept.
- Built from tables: `postal_codes`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: One code can name several places; the result is then ambiguous with ranked candidates.

### `airports`

Airport code to airport.

- Tools: `airport`
- Inputs: A code and an optional scheme (iata, icao, gps, local or ident). Without a scheme, IATA then ICAO are searched. The local scheme needs a country.
- Built from tables: `airports`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: Ambiguous codes return ranked candidates; a country narrows them.

### `locode`

UN/LOCODE to trade or transport location (port, airport, rail or road terminal).

- Tools: `locode`
- Inputs: The five-character code (two country letters and three letters or digits), or three characters plus a country.
- Built from tables: `trade_locations`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: Conflicting or malformed country hints are invalid input.

### `phone`

International telephone number to the longest published calling prefix and its country.

- Tools: `phone`
- Inputs: A number in E.164 form with a leading plus and 1 to 15 digits; spaces, hyphens and parentheses after the plus are ignored.
- Built from tables: `phone_prefixes`, `phone_metadata`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: This is prefix lookup, not subscriber validation. Shared calling codes such as +1 return one candidate per country.

### `ip`

IPv4 or IPv6 address to the published geolocation interval that contains it.

- Tools: `ip`
- Inputs: A bare address literal; ports, CIDR suffixes and IPv6 zones are invalid.
- Built from tables: `ip_ranges`, `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: The point is the provider's location for the interval, usually a city centre, not the device.

### `plates`

Vehicle registration plate text to the countries, and sometimes the region, whose recorded formats it fits.

- Tools: `plate`
- Inputs: Plate text and an optional country and series.
- Built from tables: `places`, `canonical_cities`, `place_to_city`, `countries`, `subdivisions`
- Notes: Format evidence, not a vehicle registry. Without a country the result is usually ambiguous across countries.

## Tools

Every tool is read-only, never installs data and never uses the network. Lookup tools return the result object described below.

### `reverse`

Find the country, subdivision, city and timezone at a latitude and longitude.

Needs the core pack. status is matched when stored land covers the point
and not_found otherwise: open water, land outside the installed coverage,
or unassigned land. match says how the city was chosen: contained (inside
a boundary), nearest (nearest settlement within the distant threshold) or
nearest_distant (farther; treat the city as approximate), and
distance_band bounds that distance in kilometres. point and cell describe
the resolution 8 H3 cell that holds the input, not the input itself. With
evidence, a miss explains itself (no_land, outside_coverage, unassigned)
and a match shows the city_method that chose the city.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lat` | number | yes |  | Latitude in degrees, -90 to 90 |
| `lon` | number | yes |  | Longitude in degrees, -180 to 180 |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `h3`

Find the stored ancestor of an H3 cell at resolution zero to eight.

Needs the core pack. Like reverse, from a cell instead of a point.
Cells of resolution 3 to 8 search themselves and their stored ancestors;
resolutions 0 to 2 have no stored ancestor and return not_found. A
resolution above 8 or a malformed cell is invalid_input.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cell` | string | yes |  | H3 cell as 15 hexadecimal characters, resolution 0 to 8 |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `geocode`

Finds towns and cities by name. Street addresses are not supported.

Needs the core pack. status is matched for one city and ambiguous when
several share the name: candidates are ranked by population and the
flat fields keep only what every candidate shares. Pass country or
subdivision to narrow them, or prefer="population" to take the largest.
match is exact, alternate_name (a published English or other name) or
fuzzy (typo tolerant; check the returned name). A street address is
unsupported_granularity.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes |  | City or town name, not an address |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country code; a hard filter |
| `subdivision` | string or null | no | `null` | Subdivision code such as US-IL; a hard filter |
| `limit` | integer | no | `5` | Most candidates to return, 1 to 100 |
| `prefer` | string or null | no | `null` | "population" picks the most populous of several cities |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `postal`

Find a postal code in the required source country.

Needs the postal pack. Spaces are ignored; hyphens and leading zeros are
kept. A code that names several places is ambiguous: candidates are
ranked by population. A malformed country, such as a country name
instead of its two-letter code, is invalid_input.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | yes |  | The code to look up; leading zeros matter |
| `country` | string | yes |  | Two-letter country code of the postal system |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `airport`

Find an airport by IATA/ICAO or a specified code scheme.

Needs the airports pack. The point is the airport's own point and the
city is the canonical city around it, which can differ from the name in
the airport's title. The local scheme needs a country; an unknown scheme
is invalid_input. A code shared by several airports is ambiguous.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | yes |  | The code to look up; leading zeros matter |
| `scheme` | string or null | no | `null` | iata, icao, gps, local or ident; omit for IATA then ICAO |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country code; narrows ambiguous codes |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `locode`

Find a trade location by its five-character LOCODE.

Needs the locode pack. Evidence carries the function flags, status and
remarks. A malformed code or a conflicting country is invalid_input; an
unknown code is not_found.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | yes |  | UN/LOCODE, e.g. BEANR, or three characters with country |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country code when the code has three characters |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `phone`

Find the longest published prefix of an international E.164 number.

Needs the phone pack. This is prefix lookup, not subscriber validation.
A calling code shared by several countries, such as +1, can be
ambiguous with one candidate per country unless country narrows it. A
number without the leading plus is invalid_input.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `number` | string | yes |  | E.164 number with a leading plus and 1 to 15 digits |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country code; narrows a shared calling code |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `ip`

Find published context for an IPv4 or IPv6 literal.

Needs the ip pack. The answer is the geolocation provider's location for
the interval that contains the address, usually a city centre; it is not
the location of the device. An address outside the published intervals, for
example a loopback address, is not_found.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | yes |  | IPv4 or IPv6 address literal, without port or mask |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `plate`

Find recorded registration formats, preserving country ambiguity.

Needs the plates pack. The result is format evidence, not a vehicle
registry. Without a country, plates usually fit formats of several
countries and the result is ambiguous with candidates ranked by evidence
(rank_basis). With a country the answer is that country, and evidence
explains how much geography the code supports.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes |  | Vehicle registration plate text |
| `country` | string or null | no | `null` | Two-letter country context; stays exact when given |
| `series` | string or null | no | `null` | Series or subdivision context for series-based plates |
| `evidence` | boolean | no | `false` | Add the audit evidence: why the answer or the miss, and sources |

### `describe`

Describe the open Parquet dataset behind the answers.

Without a table, lists every table with its purpose, grain, key and
number of columns. With a table, returns its columns (type, nullability,
units, meaning), primary key, joins to other tables, and the enumerated
values of coded columns. Use it before writing SQL over the dataset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `table` | string or null | no | `null` | Dataset table name; omit to list every table |

## Resources

- `thereabouts://dictionary` (application/json): Dataset tables, columns, joins and enumerations, pack families, tools and result fields. From the installed core pack when it ships one.
- `thereabouts://dictionary/markdown` (text/markdown): The same dictionary as readable Markdown.

## Result

Every lookup tool returns one result object. `evidence` appears only when requested and `hint` only when the input needs correction.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | string (values: `status`) | Typed outcome; misses and invalid query values are ordinary results |
| `kind` | string (values: `kind`) | Domain of the answer; reverse uses cell |
| `match` | string or null (values: `match`) | Published spatial method, absent for misses and invalid inputs |
| `country` | Country or null | Matched country or the country shared by every ambiguous candidate |
| `state` | State or null | Flat subdivision context, using indexed metadata |
| `city` | City or null | Final published canonical city or rural settlement |
| `timezone` | string or null | Single country-valid zone; unresolved overlap stays in evidence |
| `point` | Point or null | Representative query-cell centre for reverse lookups |
| `cell` | string or null | Canonical query H3 cell; coarse inputs retain their own resolution |
| `distance_band` | DistanceBand or null | Published nearest-policy interval, absent for contained results |
| `candidates` | array of Result | Ranked forward candidates; reverse always leaves this empty |
| `rank_basis` | string or null (values: `rank_basis`) | Forward ranking rule, absent for reverse lookups |
| `evidence` | Evidence or null | Opt-in audit fields, omitted from JSON when not requested |
| `hint` | string or null | Actionable input guidance, emitted only when a query needs correction |

### `Country`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string | Published two-letter country code |
| `code3` | string or null | Published alpha-3 code, or null when unavailable |
| `name` | string | Country display name from the place catalogue |

### `State`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | string or null | Published subdivision code, falling back to the place code only if no row exists |
| `name` | string | Subdivision table name, falling back only when the row is absent |

### `City`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Stable canonical city or final rural-settlement identity |
| `name` | string | Published canonical display name; never reconstructed by the client |
| `name_en` | string or null | English name when the dataset supplies one |
| `kind` | string | Published settlement class such as city, town or village |
| `population` | integer or null | Published population, with unknown zero represented as null |
| `point` | Point or null | Published catalogue anchor, independent of the query cell centre |

### `Point`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lat` | number | Latitude in geographic degrees |
| `lon` | number | Longitude in geographic degrees |

### `DistanceBand`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `greater_than_km` | number | Exclusive lower policy bound in kilometres |
| `at_most_km` | number | Inclusive upper policy bound in kilometres |

### `Evidence`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stored_cell` | string or null | Stored pack ancestor, possibly split by a timezone boundary |
| `country_id` | string or null | Country catalogue identity behind the spatial label |
| `state_id` | string or null | Subdivision catalogue identity behind the spatial label |
| `city_id` | string or null | Final city or settlement identity behind the spatial label |
| `city_method` | string or null (values: `cells.city_method`) | Original golden assignment method, when a city is assigned |
| `land_method` | string or null (values: `cells.land_method`) | Published land or offshore eligibility marker |
| `reason` | string or null (values: `evidence.reason`) | Detailed matched or not-found reason without changing public status |
| `timezones` | array of string | Unresolved zone survivors after country narrowing; empty for a unique zone |
| `source_ids` | array of objects or null | Source identifiers published in the city catalogue evidence |

### `status`

- `matched`: Published geography or one resolved place
- `ambiguous`: Several ranked places; flat fields retain only candidate consensus
- `not_found`: No stored answer for the query
- `invalid_input`: The query cannot be interpreted in this domain
- `unsupported_granularity`: The input requests detail finer than the dataset supports

### `kind`

- `city`: A canonical city or rural settlement
- `cell`: A spatial cell, including country-only reverse context
- `postal`: A postal code with a published anchor
- `airport`: An airport identified by a supported code
- `trade_location`: A port or other transport location
- `ip_range`: A published IP address interval
- `phone_prefix`: A published calling-code or telephone prefix
- `plate`: A vehicle registration format or series

### `match`

- `exact`: An exact normalized identifier or primary name
- `alternate_name`: A published English or alternate name
- `fuzzy`: A fuzzy name-index match
- `contained`: The dataset publishes polygon or area containment
- `nearest`: The published nearest-distance band below the distant threshold
- `nearest_distant`: The published nearest-distance band above the distant threshold

### `evidence.reason`

- `matched` (reverse, h3): A stored cell supplied the geography
- `unassigned` (reverse, h3): A stored cell exists but has no country, subdivision or city; the status is not_found
- `no_land` (reverse, h3): The cell's block is in the pack but no land is stored at this resolution 8 cell, as in open water. In a subset pack it means no admitted land row, not a global ocean assertion
- `outside_coverage` (reverse, h3): The cell's block is not in the pack, so the point is outside the pack's coverage
- `no_stored_ancestor` (reverse, h3): A coarse H3 query (resolution 0 to 7) has no stored cell at or above it
- `name_exact` (geocode): The normalized query equals a canonical or alternate city name
- `name_prefix` (geocode): No exact name; the query is the start of a city name
- `name_trigram` (geocode): No exact or prefix name; an approximate (fuzzy) name match
- `exact_code` (postal, airport, locode, phone, ip): The normalized code or address equals an indexed key or falls in an indexed interval
- `country_from_key` (postal): The postal observation has no linked geography, so its country comes from the country in the lookup key; no subdivision or city is inferred
- `plate_country_inferred` (plate): No country was supplied; this candidate country was inferred from format evidence and no finer geography is returned
- `empty_or_too_long_input` (plate): The plate text was empty after normalization or longer than the policy maximum
- `known_registration_code` (plate): The code is a known registration code for the place or places listed in the evidence
- `known_state_code_no_finer_verified_unit` (plate): The code identifies a state-level registration unit and no finer verified unit
- `unknown_code_or_unverified_temporal_scope` (plate): The format fits, but the code is not a known registration code or its dates are unverified, so only the country is returned
- `no_matching_format` (plate): No recorded plate format of the country matches the text
- `subdivision_series_context_required` (plate): The country issues plates by subdivision series; pass series to narrow the geography
- `non_geographic_or_ambiguous_series` (plate): A matching format carries no geographic code or is ambiguous, so no geography is returned

### `rank_basis`

- `population` (geocode, postal, airport, locode, phone, ip): Candidates are ordered by city population, largest first, with a stable order for ties
- `plate_evidence` (plate): Candidate countries are ordered by format evidence and a vehicle-registration prior
- `plate_evidence_without_vehicle_prior` (plate): Candidate countries are ordered by format evidence alone because the pack has no vehicle prior

### Error codes

- `closed_geocoder`: An operation was attempted after closing a geocoder
- `corrupt_pack`: A pack's checksum, record, or inventory failed validation
- `data_not_installed`: No core pack is installed in the selected store
- `geocoder_error`: Base class for offline geocoder failures
- `incompatible_data`: The selected pack requires a different reader or family
- `internal_error`: A library invariant failed, such as a poisoned lock; please report it
- `invalid_input`: A value could not be encoded or looked up; the pack itself is fine
- `pack_not_found`: An explicitly selected pack directory does not exist
- `resource_limit`: The process ran out of file descriptors; raise the open-file limit
- `writer_error`: A staging or output operation failed during dataset export
- `writer_input_error`: Dataset input, options or staging state prevents export
